newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon ceasefire monitors meet in Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon ceasefire monitors meet in Lebanon.

text.p: A committee monitoring a ceasefire accord in Lebanon on Tuesday resumed discussing a complaint about Israeli shelling of civilian areas, Lebanese officials said.
They said representatives of the five nations on the committee -- France, Syria, Lebanon, Israel and the United States -- met in the coastal town of Naqoura.
Israel said it would complain to the committee, which met for four hours on Sunday, that Hizbollah guerrillas fired on its forces from three villages in south Lebanon on Thursday.
Two Israeli soldiers were killed and eight wounded on that day. Two Hizbollah guerrillas were also killed in the fighting.
Witnesses said about 50 Israeli shells slammed into two villages in the Hizbollah-held Iqlim al-Toufah ridge. A civilian woman was hurt by flying debris.
Tuesday's meeting was the fifth of the committee set up to deal with violations of a U.S.-brokered ceasefire that ended a 17-day Israeli blitz on Lebanon in April.

The ceasefire understanding bans firing from or at civilian targets on both sides of the border. But it does not prohibit guerrilla attacks on Israeli forces occupying south Lebanon and gives both sides the right to self-defence.
Hizbollah (Party of God) fighters, who have killed 20 Israeli soldiers this year in south Lebanon, are fighting to oust Israeli forces from their 15-km (nine-mile)-deep occupation zone.
